---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Pest Control"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Biological pest control is valued as the extra yield natural enemies provide on organically
managed cropland, at the organic producer price. The base year is 2019.

⚠ The scope is organic agriculture only, by design: the underlying evidence measures the yield
effect of predators where synthetic pesticides are absent, and no comparable estimate exists
for conventional systems. The full value is attributed to nature -- no human-input adjustment
(lambda) is applied, unlike the neighbouring crop rows.

## Quantity

Organic production per crop and country: FiBL's organic area extract, times the country's
conventional FAOSTAT yield, times an organic-to-conventional yield ratio per FAO crop group
(`pest_control_yield_ratio_*`). FiBL aggregate rows with no FAOSTAT production analogue are
excluded and their share logged, never guessed.

## Price

The organic producer price: the country's FAOSTAT 2019 producer price for the crop (the item's
global median where the country reports none), times the organic-to-conventional price premium
(`pest_control_price_premium`).

## Valuation

Per crop $i$, country $j$:

$$
\text{Value}_{ij} = \left(e^{\text{lnRR}_{g(i)}} - 1\right) \; A_{ij} \; y_{ij} \, r_{g(i)} \; p_{ij} \, \pi
$$

where $\text{lnRR}_{g(i)}$ is the crop group's meta-analytic log response ratio
(`pest_control_effect_lnrr_*`: the cereal effect for cereals, the vegetable effect for
vegetables, oilseeds and pulses, the other-crops effect for fruit, nuts and stimulants, zero
for every other group), $A$ the organic area, $y$ the conventional yield, $r$ the yield ratio,
$p$ the producer price and $\pi$ the price premium. Countries sum over crops; the published
table carries all 250 account countries with NA where nothing is valued.

The committed `pest_control_gep.csv` is carried beside the result as the comparison anchor. It
is a Monte Carlo mean from a pipeline that is not on the drive, so the run log reports coverage
and log-rank agreement rather than a to-the-cent match, and the total scales linearly in $\pi$
(the committed level corresponds closely to $\pi = 1$).

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `pest_control` service key:
the FiBL area extract, the FAOSTAT 2019 yield and price slices, the FAO/CPC crop
classification, the three effect sizes, the six yield ratios, the price premium and the
committed reference, each with a source row beside it.
